item.title: Church College edge SVC 31-29 to win U15 Boys title
item.description: The Church College Fiji Under 15 Boys have kept their winning ways, holding out a determined Swami Vivekananda College side 31-29. John Vugakoto led his SVC boys from the front getting in about 5 dunks as well as sinking a few threes always keeping his team in the game.
item.content:encoded:
The Church College Fiji Under 15 Boys have kept their winning ways, holding out a determined Swami Vivekananda College side 31-29.

John Vugakoto led his SVC boys from the front getting in about 5 dunks as well as sinking a few threes always keeping his team in the game.

On the Church College side, the Levaci brothers teamed up with Mausio Taliu to keep SVC in check.

Things got really serious in the dying minutes as both sides traded the lead several times.

The points were drawn at 29-all with a few seconds to go, when one of the Taliu brothers ran the ball down the side but eventually got fouled by Vugakoto, giving him two freethrows and sealing the win for the boys from Tamavua.

In the Under 17 Girls final, Yat Sen thumped Saint Joseph's Secondary School 15-3.

It went down to the wire in the Under 19 Boys semifinals of the 2026 Vodafone Fiji Secondary School Championship between Suva Grammar School and Swami Vivekananda College.

SVC eventually won 28-26 against Grammar.

Both teams were tied 11-all at halftime.

In the second half, both teams came out firing as the lead continued to change. In the other Under 19 semifinal Yat Sen defeated Church College Fiji 29-21.

item.title: Champions Ba end Extra Premier League season with 1-0 win over Rewa
item.description: Dayal’s Sawmillers Ba FC have signed off their championship-winning 2026 Extra Premier League season with a 1-0 victory over Stratum Rewa FC at their home ground. Rusiate Doidoi scored the only goal for Ba to secure the win in front of their home supporters.
item.content:encoded:
Dayal’s Sawmillers Ba FC have signed off their championship-winning 2026 Extra Premier League season with a 1-0 victory over Stratum Rewa FC at their home ground.

Rusiate Doidoi scored the only goal for Ba to secure the win in front of their home supporters.

Ba had already secured the league title before today’s match, ending a seven-year wait for the national league championship.

The champions had to work hard for the result after Etonia Dogalau was sent off, leaving Ba with 10 players for the remainder of the match.

Rewa finishes the 2026 Extra Premier League season in third place, while Extra Supermarket Labasa finished runners-up.

Both Ba and Rewa will now turn their attention to the Extra Battle of the Giants, which kicks start from next weekend.

item.title: Junior Bula Boys ready for FIFA U20 World Cup qualification bid
item.description: The Junior Bula Boys are ready to step onto the international stage and represent Fiji at the OFC U19 Men’s Championship in Samoa. The young players have been told to embrace the pressure and responsibility that comes with wearing the national jersey as they prepare to take on the region’s best in their bid to qualify for the FIFA U20 World Cup.
item.content:encoded:
The Junior Bula Boys are ready to step onto the international stage and represent Fiji at the OFC U19 Men’s Championship in Samoa.

The young players have been told to embrace the pressure and responsibility that comes with wearing the national jersey as they prepare to take on the region’s best in their bid to qualify for the FIFA U20 World Cup.

Fiji U19 Men’s National Team Head of Delegation Surend Prasad says the team is prepared for the challenge and believes the players have what it takes to represent the country with pride.

Speaking during the team’s official presentation and jersey handover, Prasad says the Junior Bula Boys understand that the road ahead will not be easy, with pressure, challenges and difficult matches expected.

He says the team has prepared well and is travelling to Samoa with a purpose — to compete, perform and create its own history in the tournament.

Prasad reminds the players that wearing the national jersey carries a responsibility to their families, Fiji FA and football supporters across the country.

He says the tournament is an opportunity for the young players to make their mark, showcase their talent and introduce themselves to the wider football world.

Prasad says talent alone will not be enough and the players will need discipline, dedication, commitment, maturity, teamwork, courage and belief.

He also acknowledged Head Coach Marika Rodu and his support staff for their work in preparing the squad and thanked the parents and guardians for the sacrifices they have made to support the players.

Fiji will face Vanuatu next Wednesday at 12pm in their opening pool match before taking on New Zealand next Saturday at 4pm.

The winner and runner-up will qualify for the FIFA U-20 World Cup 2027 in Azerbaijan and Uzbekistan.

item.title: Epic comeback sends Church College U15 boys into basketball final
item.description: The Church College Fiji Under-15 boys made an epic comeback to clinch their finals spot in the 2026 Vodafone Fiji Secondary Schools Basketball Championship when they defeated Marist Brothers High School 27-17. A strong comeback led by Mausio Taliu rallied the Tamavua side as they went full-court press and converted Marist mistakes into points to secure the win.
item.content:encoded:
The Church College Fiji Under-15 boys made an epic comeback to clinch their finals spot in the 2026 Vodafone Fiji Secondary Schools Basketball Championship when they defeated Marist Brothers High School 27-17.

A strong comeback led by Mausio Taliu rallied the Tamavua side as they went full-court press and converted Marist mistakes into points to secure the win.

In the other Under 15 semifinal, Swami Veikananda College edged International School Suva 22-20.

In other games played this morning, the Yat Sen Secondary Under 17 boys side are through to the finals this afternoon after edging Suva Grammar School 25-23.

In the girls Under 17 quarterfinals this morning, Grammar are through to the semifinals after beating Gospel High School 25-21, while Swami Veikananda College edged Nadi neighbour Fiji Agape Mission School 24-23.

item.title: Jone Wesele named new Vodafone Fiji Bulikula coach
item.description: Jone Wesele has been named the new Vodafone Fiji Bulikula Coach this afternoon. Fiji National Rugby League Chair Rajesh Singh says Wesele will be assisted by Fiji Bati Head Coach Mick Potter, Shane Morris and Joe Rabele.
item.content:encoded:
Jone Wesele has been named the new Vodafone Fiji Bulikula Coach this afternoon.

Fiji National Rugby League Chair Rajesh Singh says Wesele will be assisted by Fiji Bati Head Coach Mick Potter, Shane Morris and Joe Rabele.

Wesele says it is extremely humbling to take on the role.

He says his immediate priority is the announcement of the 40-member squad for the Women's Rugby League World Cup in Australia in October.

The new coach says his immediate focus will also be on connecting with the coaching staff and players.

The Vodafone Fiji Bulikula will be making their Rugby League World Cup debut and are pooled with New Zealand, France and Papua New Guinea.

item.title: Shankar to lead Fiji at OFC U19 Men’s Championship
item.description: Delon Shankar has been named captain of the Fiji side for the OFC U-19 Men’s Championship 2026 in Samoa. Shankar says he is honoured and proud to lead the national side and is grateful to the officials and coaches for trusting him with the responsibility.
item.content:encoded:
Delon Shankar has been named captain of the Fiji side for the OFC U-19 Men’s Championship 2026 in Samoa.

Shankar says he is honoured and proud to lead the national side and is grateful to the officials and coaches for trusting him with the responsibility.

The young defender says he is ready to lead the side to victory and hopes to make Fiji and their families proud.

The OFC U-19 Men’s Championship 2026 will be held in Samoa from next Tuesday to 14th September.

Defending champions New Zealand have been drawn alongside Tahiti, Fiji and Vanuatu in Group B, while hosts Samoa are joined by 2024 runners-up New Caledonia, Solomon Islands and Papua New Guinea in Group A.

Fiji will face Vanuatu next Wednesday at 12pm in their opening pool match before taking on New Zealand next Saturday at 4pm.

Their final pool match will be against Tahiti on 8th September at 12pm at the Samoa Football HQ.

The winner and runner-up will qualify for the FIFA U-20 World Cup 2027 in Azerbaijan and Uzbekistan.
